name: Lemnian
world_status: accessible description is silent on stress

sources.citation: Marchesini, Simona. 2024. Retico, Etrusco e Lemnio. Scenari ricostruttivi. In S. Marchesini (ed.), Rhaeti & Co. Nuovi scenari sulla questione tirrenica, 29-72. Verona: Alteritas Academy Press. DOI 10.60973/RHAETIMARCHESINI (open-access e-book).
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Sec. 3.3 'La sincope', p. 47: post-tonic vowel syncope is found only in Etruscan and is 'assente in Retico e nel Lemnio'; the Etruscan syncope is explained by a strengthening of the expiratory accent on the initial syllable. Comparative table p. 46: Fonologia / Sincope: Etrusco X, Retico -, Tirrenico di Lemnos -. P. 61 repeats that syncope of post-tonic vowels is an Etruscan innovation. No statement of where Lemnian stress falls.

sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Phonology section covers only the four vowel signs. 'Comparative features' (line 38): 'several features characteristic of historical Etruscan are absent from Lemnian, as they are from Raetic: the syncope of post-tonic vowels..' citing Marchesini 2024: 29-72. No stress statement.

sources.citation: Hajnal, Ivo. 2024. The 'Tyrrhenic question' from a linguistic perspective. In S. Marchesini (ed.), Rhaeti & Co., 11-27. Verona: Alteritas Academy Press (open access, same PDF).
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: P. 13: Lemnian preserves 'the older phonetic state in the genitive of the numeral sialchvis "40", which in Etruscan leads to sealchls.. via vowel syncope'; Rhaetic 'does not show any vowel weakening or syncope of non-initial syllables'. P. 19 n. 21 reports Rigobianco 2017 on Proto-Tyrrhenic suffix accent (*-Kwa stressed on last syllable vs *-ra unstressed) — about Etruscan/Proto-Tyrrhenic, not Lemnian. No Lemnian stress statement.

sources.citation: Belfiore, Valentina. 2020. Etrusco / Etruscan. Palaeohispanica 20: 199-262 (open access).
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Mentions Lemnian only as a related corpus (Agostiniani 2012, de Simone 2012b) closer to Etruscan than Raetic; no Lemnian phonology.

sources.citation: Eichner, Heiner. 2013. Neues zur Sprache der Stele von Lemnos (Zweiter Teil). Journal of Language Relationship 10: 1-42. DOI 10.31826/jlr-2013-100104 (open access).
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Sec. 4.1.7.7 'Ausbleiben der Vokalsynkope' (the text layer) treats absence of syncope in Etruscan names like Thucer/Velthur as due to long loan vowels; for Lemnian it notes Aker keeps its e (long vowel) where Etruscan has syncopated Acrie, and posits a Lemnian syncope only in a covered final syllable (*Tavarath > *Tavarth; *Murinaial > Morinail). No statement of accent position.

sources.citation: Eichner, Heiner. 2012. Neues zur Sprache der Stele von Lemnos (Erster Teil). Journal of Language Relationship 7: 9-32. DOI 10.31826/jlr-2012-070106 (open access).
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Epigraphic re-reading and sibilant/vowel-letter discussion; a full-text search for stress/accent Akzent/Betonung/Synkope finds only Etruscan material (p. 29 zathrum syncope; Venel apocope). Nothing on Lemnian accent position.

sources.citation: Maras, Daniele F. 2008-2022. Lemnian (language page and writing-system page). Mnamon: Ancient Writing Systems in the Mediterranean, Scuola Normale Superiore. DOI 10.25429/sns.it/lettere/mnamon049.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Segmental remarks only: two sibilants, no voiced stops, no /u/-/o/ distinction (omicron used), aspirates as in Etruscan, possibly no /f/; morphological correspondences with Etruscan. Nothing on stress or accent.

sources.citation: Bonfante, Giuliano & Larissa Bonfante. 2002. The Etruscan Language: An Introduction. 2nd ed. Manchester: Manchester University Press, pp. 61-62 (Lemnos stele) and n. 23 (archive.org scanned).
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Transcribes the stele and lists Etruscan-Lemnian similarities (endings, dating formula, no voiced stops, presence of o). The initial-accent statement on pp. 80-81 is about Etruscan c. 500 BCE only; nothing on Lemnian accent.
